title: Meta releases Muse Spark Open — open weights, if you own a terabyte
summary: Meta's 816-billion-parameter Muse Spark Open ships open weights that run on linked Mac Studios, trailing Chinese open models on Meta's own table and carrying a license aimed at inference hosts. Then Anthropic embeds six METR evaluators with employee-like access and gives up its veto over what they publish.

topics: Meta Muse Spark Open (15 October 2026): 816B total / ~42B active MoE (256 experts, 8 routed per token), 1M context, text/image/audio/video in; Meta's own model-card table puts it behind GLM 5.3 and Kimi K3 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 (76.4 vs 83.9/85.0) and the Artificial Analysis index (39 vs 45/44) but ahead on MCP-Atlas (89.2) and HLE-Diamond no-tools (26.1); StrongREJECT 0.5 vs 60-86 for other open models (Meta-reported); runs on two-four M5 Ultra Mac Studios via MLX RDMA over Thunderbolt 5 (Apple: ~493GB in NVFP4, 36.7 tok/s on four machines at 8K, ~40s TTFT at 65K); 3-bit on one 512GB Mac at ~21 tok/s; KV cache ~266GB at full 1M context; reasoning cannot be turned off; Muse Model License requires a separate agreement for model-as-a-service above $20M gross revenue (vs Llama 2's 700M MAU), 'Built with Muse Spark Open' attribution, gated on legal name/DOB/corporate identifiers

Anthropic embeds METR evaluators (15 October 2026): six METR staff with company hardware, office space, internal tools roughly on par with Anthropic's risk assessment teams; employees encouraged (not required) to share; off-limits: customer data, privileged legal material, model architecture; no veto on publication, redaction only in narrow predefined categories, METR may publicly characterize redactions; three-tier evaluator ladder (SecureBio bottom tier on the CBRN chapter of the August risk report); duration and funding unstated; bank resident-examiner analogy

dives.story: Meta's Muse Spark Open on Mac Studios
dives.why_it_matters: Anyone choosing an open-weight model to self-host now has a frontier-class American option that fits on desk hardware, and needs to know where it trails, what the license catches, and what local inference actually costs in memory and latency.

It is the first embedded-evaluator arrangement actually in operation at a frontier lab, and its terms (no veto, characterizable redactions, architecture off-limits, unstated funding) are the template the other accord signatories will be measured against.

concepts_taught: why mixture-of-experts sparsity makes unified-memory desktops viable for very large models: capacity must hold all experts, but per-token memory bandwidth only pays for the active parameters, and the KV cache rather than the weights becomes the limit at long context
